correctness.rationale: From singleton propositions, each predecessor column has <=2 points; an extremal 2n-pair relation has two-element columns. Two-target propositions force any two columns to meet; a 2-uniform pairwise-intersecting family is a star or the three edges of a triangle. The full-set image must have size >=n−1, excluding triangle as soon as n>=5; the star hub is then unique and f has image size>=n−2. Conversely the image deficit |A|−|f(A)|<=n−|f(W)|<=2 proves the all-subset bound. Stirling surjections give n![C(n,2)+C(n,3)+3C(n,4)] labelled stars; the n4 triangle case contributes 4*3!S(4,3)=144 beyond 312 stars, total456. Zero distortion forces permutations. Independently enumerated all two-vertex predecessor assignments at n4 (1296) and n5 (100000), recovering 312/144 and 4200; all-subset verification was performed explicitly. No finite enumeration is used to prove n>=5 general rigidity.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks corroborate exact identities only; all-parameter assertions depend on the reconstructed proof and named published premises.
